extracted.intended_audience: public water systems, state primacy agencies, regulated entities, environmental stakeholders, and members of the public preparing comments on the proposed perchlorate NPDWR
extracted.subtask_description: A proposed National Primary Drinking Water Regulation (NPDWR) for perchlorate under the Safe Drinking Water Act specifying health-based goals, enforceable MCL options, monitoring/analytical requirements, treatment/implementation measures, public notification and compliance provisions. The page contains the rule preamble and proposed regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLG requirement (SDWA section 1412(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG) shall be set at the level that avoids adverse effects to human health, with an adequate margin of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive the MCLG based on the most sensitive population(s) to ensure statutory protection. The preamble explains an MCLG is the maximum level of a contaminant at which no known or anticipated adverse effect on health would occur, allowing an adequate margin of safety; the EPA proposes an MCLG of 20 µg/L derived from a draft reference dose of 1 μg/kg/day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of population at greater risk
rubrics_metrics.description: When deriving the MCLG, the EPA must consider effects on groups 'at greater risk of adverse health effects' from exposure than the general population (SDWA section 1412(b)(3)(C)(i)(V)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA identifies the population at greater risk for perchlorate as the offspring of iodine-deficient, hypothyroxinemic women exposed during first trimester; the MCLG is set to protect against a one-point decrease in mean IQ in that population (and thus protect the general population).

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting the MCL (feasibility and cost considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDWA requires the MCL be set 'as close to the MCLG as is feasible,' or at a level where the cost is justified by the benefits if the Administrator determines benefits do not justify costs (SDWA section 1412(b)(4)(B) and 1412(b)(6)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is proposing and soliciting comments on MCLs of 20, 40, or 80 µg/L, and explaining feasibility and benefit–cost considerations (EPA also states Administrator determined benefits do not justify costs for nationwide regulation, but proposes due to court decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Occurrence standard for regulatory determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A contaminant must be known or substantially likely to occur in public water systems with a frequency and at levels of public health concern to justify an NPDWR (SDWA section 1412(b)(1)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates both occurrence in PWSs and the health effects information to determine whether regulation presents a meaningful opportunity for health risk reduction; the preamble documents historic and recent occurrence analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of best available science and systematic review methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Health assessments and derivation of MCLG/MCL must use the best available science, consistent with EPA's peer-reviewed systematic review methods and guidance (and Executive Order 14303).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA updated its 2019 health assessment using peer-reviewed systematic review methods (USEPA, 2022b), IRIS and other guidance; the preamble emphasizes reproducibility, transparency, peer review, interdisciplinary approaches, communication of uncertainty, and avoidance of conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health risk reduction and cost analysis requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency must analyze and compare benefits and costs, perform uncertainty analysis, and make a benefit–cost determination when proposing an NPDWR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section XIV of the preamble lays out A) Comparison of Benefits and Costs, B) Uncertainty Analysis, C) Benefit–Cost Determination; EPA describes that for this proposed rule it finds benefits do not justify costs but proceeds due to judicial requirement and requests comment on analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial monitoring requirements (system type and size specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems (CWSs) and non-transient non-community water systems (NTNCWSs) must conduct specified initial monitoring for perchlorate based on source type and system size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All ground water systems serving >10,000 persons without acceptable historic data and all surface water systems without acceptable historic data must collect four initial consecutive quarterly samples at all sampling points. Ground water systems serving ≤10,000 persons without acceptable historic data must collect two initial samples between five and seven months apart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previously collected/historical data to satisfy initial monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: States may accept historical monitoring data to meet initial monitoring requirements if data meet specified criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may accept historical data for a sampling point if the water system uses monitoring data with the same number of samples specified for initial monitoring, or data collected under a state monitoring requirement between January 1, 2021 and the date of publication of the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-initial monitoring frequency rules (results-based monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent monitoring frequency depends on initial monitoring results at each sampling point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all initial samples at a sampling point are ≤4.0 µg/L → one sample per compliance cycle (nine years). Surface water systems with all initial samples ≤MCL and any above 4.0 µg/L → one sample annually. Ground water systems with all initial samples ≤MCL and any above 4.0 µg/L → one sample per compliance period (three years). Any system with initial monitoring result above MCL → monitor quarterly at that sampling point. States may increase frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring waivers / State discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority and processes for States to grant waivers or make adjustments to monitoring requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble and regulatory text ask and provide for State discretion in increasing sampling frequency, accepting historical data, and other system-specific determinations; EPA also includes a section/questioning 'Can States grant monitoring waivers?' for consideration/comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation sampling and compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If initial sample indicates an exceedance of the MCL, a confirmation sample is required and compliance is determined from averaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must take a confirmation sample within five days of receipt of analytical results of the first sample. Where a State-required confirmation sample is taken, the initial and confirmation sample results shall be averaged to determine compliance. States may delete obvious sampling errors. For nitrate, nitrite, and perchlorate, one sample is sufficient if below the MCL; if initial exceeds MCL a confirmation is required and average is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection, preservation, container, and holding time procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling must follow specified sample preservation, container, and maximum holding time procedures set out in the regulatory table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule revises table(s) specifying sample collection/preservation/containers and maximum holding times for perchlorate (and other IOCs); systems must follow these procedures when collecting compliance samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methods and incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved compliance analytical methods for perchlorate are listed in a table and are incorporated by reference; equivalent or alternative methods may be used if determined equivalent by EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 to paragraph (k) lists approved compliance methods; methods incorporated by reference were approved by the Director of the Federal Register. Alternatives listed in appendix A to subpart C or equivalent methods as determined by EPA are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses must be conducted by laboratories certified by EPA or the State; provisional certification allowed historically until January 1, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To receive certification to conduct analyses for perchlorate, laboratories must meet the certification criteria specified (analytical competence, QA/QC, etc.); analysis under this section shall only be conducted by certified labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and compliance actions for systems exceeding MCL
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems with perchlorate levels exceeding the MCL must take actions to comply, including installing treatment, using new/uncontaminated source, or connecting to an uncontaminated source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ion exchange, reverse osmosis, and biological treatment have been demonstrated to remove perchlorate to comply with proposed MCL. Certified reverse osmosis point-of-use devices are available for small systems. EPA discusses treatment technologies (section XII) and references economic analysis for system cost estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Best Available Technologies (BATs) and small-system compliance technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule identifies BATs and affordable technologies for small systems to achieve compliance with the perchlorate MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables/paragraphs add 'Biological Treatment' as a key to BATs and list Ion Exchange, Reverse Osmosis, and Biological Treatment as technologies; EPA identifies affordable technology, treatment technique, or other means for systems serving ≤10,000 persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification (PN) and Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed PN and CCR requirements to inform consumers about perchlorate in drinking water and to provide standard health effects language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices A and B to Subpart Q are amended to add perchlorate entries, including the standard health effects language for public notification and instructions for CCR content; the rule prescribes tiers and text for notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and enforcement provisions (primacy, dates, recordkeeping, reporting, exemptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules establishing compliance dates, primacy requirements for States, State recordkeeping and reporting requirements, exemption/extension processes, and availability of funding and technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule proposes effective dates (e.g., many provisions effective 3 years after final rule publication), sets out primacy responsibilities under 40 CFR part 142, state reporting and recordkeeping requirements, provisions for exemptions/extensions, and discusses funding/technical assistance availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic monitoring frequency reduction provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions to reduce monitoring burden automatically for systems based on initial sampling results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because most systems are unlikely to have perchlorate at levels of public health concern, the proposal includes provisions to automatically reduce monitoring frequency for systems with low initial results (e.g., ≤4.0 µg/L) instead of requiring case-by-case State determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averaging rules and State discretion for obvious sampling errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where confirmation samples are required, the initial and confirmation results are averaged for compliance determination; States have discretion to delete obvious sampling errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (f)(4) adds that if a State-required confirmation sample is taken, the initial and confirmation sample results shall be averaged for compliance; States may delete obvious sampling errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text incorporation and administrative approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference of methods and materials requires Director of the Federal Register approval and availability at specified repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of the Federal Register approves incorporation by reference in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51; copies of incorporated materials may be inspected at EPA's Drinking Water Docket or NARA and links are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific compliance-sampling timeliness (confirmation within 5 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness requirement for confirmation sampling when an initial sample indicates an exceedance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial sampling indicates perchlorate exceedance, the system must take a confirmation sample within five days of the system's receipt of the analytical results of the first sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions/requests for comment on compositing samples
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA poses the question whether systems can composite samples and solicits input on compositing policies and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Table of Contents and monitoring sections include 'F. Can systems composite samples?' as a topic for discussion in the proposal, indicating EPA is requesting stakeholder input on whether compositing should be allowed and under what conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of monitoring (which systems and sampling points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines which system types and sampling points are subject to initial and routine monitoring for perchlorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All groundwater systems serving >10,000 persons without acceptable historic data and all surface water systems without acceptable historic data must sample all sampling points as specified; definitions of acceptable historic data and GWUDI treatment are referenced in footnotes and text.
